review: 1:2 מִן־חַיַּי לְמָחָר — 'of my life for tomorrow'; the Arabic فِي الْغَدِ is literally 'in the morrow', and Hebrew needs the preposition to keep the 7 syllables.

2:1–2:2 — the Arabic opens stanza 2 by restating stanza 1 ('I know not what shall come tomorrow or after'); Hebrew keeps the restatement but varies the verb (לֹא אֵדַע) so the repetition does not read as a copyist's slip.
3:3–3:4 טוֹב רֵעַ / טוֹב עוֹזֵר — the Arabic repeats خَيْرُ ('best'), and Hebrew repeats טוֹב at the head of both half-lines as the tune's parallel.
3:7 שָׁם לֹא־תִזַּל דִּמְעָה — 'there no tear shall drip'; נָזַל is the biblical verb for tears running down (Job 3:24), which is stronger than a plain 'flow'.
Metre note: the printed stanza 1 is 4 lines, stanzas 2–3 are 8; the payload follows the print, so the meter script reports an irregular shape by construction.
